issue.summary: {Break} navtitle attribute is not automatically added to topicrefs in a DITA map
issue.description: When ui_config.json sets ditaAttributes.required.navtitle to true (Global or Folder Profile), a newly inserted <topicref> in the Map Editor is saved without @navtitle. Expected: every newly added <topicref> receives @navtitle populated from the referenced topic's <title> (e.g. <topicref href="topic1.dita" navtitle="Topic 1"/>), per the documented behaviour 'Include @navtitle attribute by default'. Critical bug, In UAC, component Editor, fix version 2610.

Re-test map save, validation, and reopen so navtitle does not break map serialization or DTD validation.
Re-test the generated-output navigation labels and bookmarks that consume navtitle so the auto-populated value renders correctly downstream, informed by GUIDES-10509.
Re-test existing maps opened after the fix so previously saved topicrefs are not rewritten or corrupted on open.

Re-test both navtitle-population consumers (the Insert Topic Reference dialog and the drag-and-drop path) that share the required-attribute logic, so a fix in the shared path does not regress either entry point.
Re-test reuse consumers (keyref/xref link-text resolution and topics referenced in multiple maps) so the auto-populated navtitle resolves consistently for reused content.

dita_semantics.neighbourhood_assessment: Primary construct @navtitle is derived from the referenced topic <title> (AC-02); it is governed by @locktitle, which decides whether the navtitle overrides the referenced title in navigation and output (AC-11). topichead is the href-less variant where @navtitle is the sole navigation label (AC-07); mapref derives @navtitle from the referenced map <title> (AC-08). keydef (resource-only) and glossref are specializations where required-navtitle applies differently or not at all (AC-17, AC-18), and navref and reltable are non-navigation neighbours re-tested as regression (AC-19). Reuse consumers keyref/conref and xref/link-text read the navtitle as link text, including the @navtitle attribute versus <topicmeta><navtitle> element distinction (AC-14). No further governing construct is in scope.
